summary: Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche (1933–2023) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Khenpo Gangshar (~1953–1958) and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He served as abbot at Rumtek Monastery (~1968), Karma Shri Nalanda Institute (~1981), and Gampo Abbey (~1984–2023).
Khenchen Tsewang Rigdzin studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Khenpo Appey Rinpoche (1927–2010) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dzongsar Monastery and under Dragyab Lodrö. He served as director of Sakya College from 1972 to 1985 and held a post at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
Khenpo Dazer worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and held teaching posts at Śrī Siṃha Shedra and the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute.

Khenpo Gangshar (1925–1980) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shechen Monastery (~1937–1953) under Shechen Kongtrul, Khyentse Ozer, and Karsé Kongtrul. He served as senior teacher at Shechen (~1953–1957) and founding dean at Surmang Monastery (~1957–1958).

Khenpo Jigme Phuntsok (1933–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima (~1951–1957), Yonten Gonpo, A Kya Lama Gar Chö, Pema Norbu, Khenchen Orgyen Gönpo, and several other teachers.

Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche (1924–2019) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Thrangu Monastery (~1936–1958) and under the 8th Traleg Rinpoche, Khenpo Gangshar, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught at Rumtek Monastery (1967) and was abbot of Karma Triyana Dharmachakra (1978).
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche (born 1946) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Bokar Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang (1879–1941) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Shenphen Nangwa, Kunzang Pelden, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Lungtok Tenpé Nyima (~1898–1901).
Khenpo Nüden studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin, Lama Zolpa Trinlé, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1960–1981). He served as principal shedra teacher at Rumtek Monastery (~1977) and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery (1992).

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jetsun Lochen Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Kangyur Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and others. He taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970) and the University of Virginia (~1974–1975).

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Rumtek Monastery and under Rasvir Das, Dev Narayan Tripathi, Shenphen Nangwa, and others. He taught at Men-Tsee-Khang in Lhasa and held a teaching post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
Khyenrab Norbu (1882–1962) was active in Tibetology and other fields. He studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen.

id: P:Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé
summary: Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, where he is attested in 1983 and attested as professor emeritus in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon works in Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Otago under Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie (attested 2015), and studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, John Kieschnick, Barend J. ter Haar, and Seishi Karashima in 2013.

Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher. He studied at the First Higher School (1903), University of Tokyo (~1906–1909), and University of Freiburg (1920). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1911–1918; 1923–1945), Hokkaido University (1947; 1950–1951), and Chuo University (1951–1958).
